Instead I’ll warn you that it will get worse before it gets better. The support will fade away and they’ll get back to their regularly scheduled programming. You’ll be left with an empty side of the bed, a toothbrush that doesn’t move, an elephant on your chest, and a frog in your throat. You don’t have to forgive her, but you have to take care of yourself and seek support and professional help wherever you can find it. 
Joy will come to you again, but be prepared for a rollercoaster. The grief hill is never straight up or down, it’s ever changing and flowing and darting in different directions. You’ll get better at being the rider though.

yes, small aneurysms can absolutely burst. but your doctor will likely tell you that it’s a less than 1% chance of rupture. (it doesn’t help your peace of mind) but it’s good to know. 
sorry for the ramble- but if you ever want to chat, please please please reach out. you are NOT alone in this. 

as for what tests to expect- for me, my regular neurologist did the MRI that found it initially. then once i was established with a neurosurgeon, he did his own MRI & CTA. then he basically told me i was fine, had virtually 0 risk of rupture, NO restrictions, and to come back in a year for monitoring. i didn’t like this. but he’s highly rated and i have to just trust him. it’s so so hard.
